The main takeaway from our work is that

the baryon-poor fluid, which is produced in heavy-ion collisions at intermediate incident energies, can be well described as an independent fluid, without the need for an explicit interaction with baryon-rich matter.

the baryon free fluid, as a new dynamical degree of freedom, has the potential to significantly improve the description of heavy-ion collisions at intermediate energies, where the baryon density is low.

the baryon number of the midrapidity fluid is conserved, even in a scenario where the baryon density of this fluid is zero, provided that a finite formation time is introduced for the baryonfree fluid.
